text:
maria: quick check — seeing odd interplay between stop sequences and max_tokens in our contract tests. when streaming, stop sometimes arrives after we hit max_tokens and we get an extra token + finish_reason=\"length\". payload + observed below, anyone seen this? cc @kevin @jen

kevin: can you paste the exact response snippet you saw? streaming vs non-streaming matters.

maria: pasted minimal repro (obfuscated):
```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  \"model\": \"open-compat-test\",
  \"prompt\": \"Write a line and then STOP_SEQUENCE\",
  \"max_tokens\": 12,
  \"stop\": [\"STOP_SEQUENCE\"],
  \"temperature\": 0.0,
  \"top_p\": 0.9,
  \"logprobs\": 5,
  \"stream\": true
}
```
Observed stream final chunk (assembled):
```json
{
  \"choices\": [
    {
      \"text\": \"... some text STOP_SEQUENCE extra\",
      \"finish_reason\": \"length\",
      \"logprobs\": null
    }
  ]
}
```
Notes: stop sequence present in final text (so stop applied) but finish_reason shows \"length\" and logprobs null even though request asked for logprobs. tokens/logprobs alignment also looked off.

jen: interesting — deterministic semantics note: temp=0 is only fully deterministic if top_p==1.0. With top_p<1 you still do nucleus sampling (stochastic), so combine temp=0 + top_p<1 is not guaranteed deterministic. that aside, logprobs should still be returned when requested.

alex: runtime quirk we saw before: streaming path flushes a buffered token before checking stop criteria which can yield an extra token. if that flush triggers max_tokens we end up with finish_reason=\"length\".

tim: from an API contract POV we should define precise expectations: does stop take precedence over max_tokens? should logprobs be present when finish_reason=\"length\"? and what do we guarantee for streaming partials?

sophie: CI: test gf-2145 failing on main (genparams/stop-vs-length-logprobs). failure: expected non-null logprobs when logprobs requested.

ci-bot: [CI] gf-2145 failed — details: https://ci.internal/redwood/builds/8892 (artifact contains response snippets).

kevin: proposed contract wording (draft):
- stop sequences are applied to the generated token stream as soon as they are emitted; if a stop is produced before max_tokens is reached, finish_reason == \"stop\" and returned token count <= max_tokens.
- if max_tokens limit is hit first, finish_reason == \"length\".
- logprobs: if client requests logprobs, the response must include a logprobs object aligned to the returned tokens regardless of finish_reason (unless model cannot provide them for technical reasons, in which case server must set a warning header).
- streaming: final chunk must contain the token that triggers stop and then close the stream; no extra tokens after stop.

jen: +1 to that contract. small tweak: clarify that deterministic sampler is defined as (temperature==0 AND top_p==1 AND top_k==0) — otherwise behavior may be stochastic. add a note for SDKs.

alex: implementation plan: patch streaming runtime so we check stop conditions before flushing buffered token. that should prevent the extra token. i'll open a PR and add a unit test `stream_stop_before_length`.

tim: please also add an integration contract test for the contract-suite that sends both stream and non-stream requests with the stop near the max_tokens boundary.

maria: repro added to the internal testcase repo (non-prod). linking here once uploaded.

ci-bot: PR #4521 opened by alex: \"fix(runtime): check stop before flush in streaming path\" — https://git.internal/p/4521

alex: assigning the runtime change to myself, eta: EOD tomorrow. adding unit + integration tests.

kevin: i'll write the contract-suite test and the API doc wording, pinging @jen for the deterministic sampler blurb.

jen: will draft doc text this afternoon and attach to PR.

sophie: note for release: if runtime change alters behavior for edge cases we should include a note in 1.8.1 and flag customers who pin models.

maria: thanks everyone — ping here when PR merges so i can re-run gf-2145. :thumbsup:
